newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Target stake in Malaysia gold mine up.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Target stake in Malaysia gold mine up.

text.p: Target Resources Australia NL said on Thursday it had raised its interest in gold production from the Selingsing mine project in Malaysia by a further 9.75 percent.
Target said it also entered into an agreement to acquire a further 2.5 percent interest in the southern lease at Selingsing.

Target said the acquisitions, from its joint venture partners, would give it an interest in 62.5 percent of the cash flow from the mine's southern lease and 59.75 percent of the cash flow from the northern lease.

Target said as consideration for the 9.75 percent interest it would pay a total of A$6 million, comprising A$2 million cash with the balance of A$4 million to be satisfied by the issue of shares in Mining Corp of Australia Ltd (MCA).
Target is currently in the process of merging with MCA.
Target said the shares would issued at 80 percent of market price at the date of issue.

"Should the merger with MCA not proceed for any reason, the balance will be satisfied by the issue of shares in Target Resources at 80 percent of the market price at the date of issue," the company said in a statement.
The company said the additional 9.75 percent share of production would be paid to the company by way of management fee for its services as manager to the project.
"The agreement provides that Target will remain as manager for the life of the mine provided Target continues to hold not less than 50 percent of the production interest," Target said.

Target said the separate deal to buy the extra 2.5 percent of the southern lease, from Syed Kharul Azhu Bin Syed, would cost it four million ringgit, of which three million would in cash and one million in MCA or Target shares.
At 2.00 p.m. (0300 GMT), Target shares were two cents weaker at 24.5 cents while MCA shares were 11 cents lower at A$1.90.
